english.title: Cause / permit keeper of conventionally reared meat chickens to fail to hold certificate - England
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without lawful authority or excuse, caused or permitted a person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), who was responsible for conventionally reared meat chickens at **(..SPECIFY PREMISES..), the keeper not to comply with the duty to be the holder of a certificate recognised by the Secretary of State for the purposes of Article 4(3) or (4) of Council Directive 2007/43/EC (certificates of completion of training courses or equivalent experience)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 5(1)(ba), 7(1)(c) and 9 of, and paragraph 2 of Schedule 5A to, the Welfare of Farmed Animals (England) Regulations 2007.

english.standardstatementoffacts: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant, without lawful authority or excuse, caused or permitted a person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), who was responsible for conventionally reared meat chickens at **(..SPECIFY PREMISES..), the keeper not to comply with the duty to be the holder of a certificate recognised by the Secretary of State for the purposes of Article 4(3) or (4) of Council Directive 2007/43/EC (certificates of completion of training courses or equivalent experience).

other.penalty:
Summary: 51 weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level four on the standard scale.

Note
In relation to an offence committed before section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 comes into force, the reference to 51 weeks imprisonment in relation to summary offences, above, is to be read as a reference to 6 months imprisonment.
